method: cross-entropy search over parameters minimising 10-step open-loop replay error of block pose (pos + 60 u/rad * angle) on all segments where the block moves; pusher gains fitted first on 5-step pusher replays. Values per fit: [life1 only, life2 only, lives 1+2].

mechanisms.name: M1 pusher_pd
mechanisms.evidence: step-command and ramp responses in life 1 (steps 0-67); replay error 0.01-0.02 u. Pusher velocity is not changed by contact (life 1 steps 68-80 constant 28.7,-22.5 u/s) -> the pusher is kinematic w.r.t. the block.

mechanisms.name: M3 centre_of_mass (UNUSUAL)
mechanisms.evidence: axial push on the stem tip turned the block -18 deg in 13 steps (life 1, steps 68-81); independent fits on life 1 and life 2 agree within 1 u; replay loss with the COM forced to the drawing centroid is 7x larger (life 1: 3.06 vs 0.41).
mechanisms.conclusion: the block's mass is concentrated toward the right end of the bar (+u) and lower than the drawn centroid: COM ~ (24, 30) instead of (0, 40.7). Pushes through the drawn centroid therefore rotate the block (counter-intuitive to a planner using the drawing).

mechanisms.name: M3 radius_of_gyration
mechanisms.evidence: rotation rate vs translation in contact segments; spread 50-56 across fits

mechanisms.name: M2 contact
mechanisms.evidence: contact friction converges to ~0 in every fit (the pusher slides along faces); restitution small and poorly determined (0-0.1)

mechanisms.name: M4 table_friction
mechanisms.evidence: release-and-watch phases (life 1 steps 81-90 etc.): the block keeps sliding after the pusher leaves, displacement per step shrinking geometrically (~x0.63/step) -> mostly viscous decay (~4.6/s), small Coulomb part

mechanisms.name: M5 walls
mechanisms.evidence: task_card only; never exercised in the lives (no wall contact observed) -> crude clamp

unusual: The block's centre of mass is offset ~24 u to the +u side of the symmetry axis and ~11 u below the drawn centroid; it also coasts after release (inertia + viscous floor friction) and the pusher-block contact is nearly frictionless.
uncertainty: CEM elite spreads are over-confident; the spread across the three independent fits is the honest uncertainty (see per_fit). Not represented stochastically in the planner (the open-loop error is ~0.6 u / 0.4 deg after 20 steps).

object_L.evidence_for_carry_over: on L life 1 refitting ALL parameters lowers the 10-step replay loss only from 0.217 (mass + mu refit, rest from the T) to 0.195; the free pusher fit gives kp 100.4, kv 20.1 (T: 100, 20)

evidence.com: fits with different free sets: com_u 22.8-23.6, com_v 54.2-57.2 (L life 1, and lives 1+2 wall-free); COM at the drawn centroid raises the loss 0.22 -> 0.79
evidence.k_gyr: 83-101 across fits (uniform L would be ~40): the L turns sluggishly; partly traded against mu
evidence.mu: L life 1 is flat for mu >= 0.36 and bad at 0 (0.65 vs 0.22); L life 2 wall-free windows have a minimum at 0.36 -> 0.4, plausible 0.3-1. The T's contact was frictionless (mu ~ 0)

object_L.unusual: like the T, the L's mass is off its drawn centroid (here ~14 u toward the leg side and ~13 u up), it has a large rotational inertia, and -- unlike the T -- the pusher grips it (contact friction ~0.4). 'Same batch' held for the pusher and the floor, not for contact friction or mass distribution.
object_L.walls: M5 (hard clamp) is badly wrong: on life 2 the real block was pushed up to 25 u through the top wall and later ejected at ~25 u/step; 5-step replay error near walls 28 u mean vs 4 u (median 0.5 u) away from walls. Not fixed in the world; the planner was given a wall-clearance cost instead.
